pr_title: Improve UI scaling on iOS devices
pr_body:
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/7012

Been playing around with this on my iPhone 12 and iOS simulators, and applying a general 2x scale makes the game looks pretty fitting on all iOS devices according to the simulator.

Before:
![CleanShot 2022-12-24 at 00 01 51](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/209409543-2c6a5755-943c-4003-891a-33c48b95bc54.png)

After:
![CleanShot 2022-12-23 at 23 52 04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/209409550-bc62b1d0-1dce-40d5-8b79-25c8f618c51b.png)
pr_comments:
This won't work as a blanket change like this. It should probably be based on the DPI scale of the screen, not the device flag. If the best we can do is a device type flag, this change should be limited to phones, and not cover tablets.

Here's how it looks on an iPad:

![2B99920F-A5FB-472F-AEBA-2E30E743C6B8](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/202914366-135ee816-1d38-48ed-9a11-aced300eabb5.jpeg)

Ignoring the fact it's leaving the screen, it feels too big. I actually use <1x on my ipad for reference.

Aspect ratio of the device will also play a factor here. The root scaling container of the game is assuming 16:9, while the iPad shown above seems closer to 4:3, causing the sides to leave the screen.

In effort of potentially pushing osu! to the app store, I've came back to this PR and experimented with it for a bit (see https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21335#issue-1456964765). TL;DR: Having osu! scale based on the screen resolution doesn't really work well on iOS since it's not based on a resizable window like desktop platforms. Instead, applying a general constant scale works mostly better on all iOS devices (@peppy check how it feels on your iPad now, the default scale should be slightly smaller than on master).

I've also covered Android here, but I don't have a physical device myself to tell if it looks big or not (and emulators aren't really helping, since there's no way to determine the physical size), checking on a phone and a tablet and potentially tuning the constant scale there would be appreciated.

That being said, the beatmap details area in song select need relayout or scroll support because, on my iPhone, the rating spread is cut off and the points of failure is completely masked below the screen. I have no earthly idea of how to make it look better. Ideas would be appreciated.
@frenzibyte Hoping to revisit this and get it in. Could you please rebase or do something about the weird changes in the diff? 😅

Taking a step back here, I'm pretty sure you don't want this kind of complex logic. Instead, you'd be looking to find a static value to replace `1024x768` that works better for mobile. Or failing that, rather than adding complex logic to only the iOS implementation, I think it would be better to change the way scaling works across *all* platforms.

Like, there's no reason iOS should get its own exclusive behaviour. Desktop devices could also be similar DPI / screen ratios and should be able to display just as well with default settings.

I'm in favour of spending some more time on this until it makes sense visually and code-wise.

In that case I'll start off by closing this PR because there was no sane way I have figured out from the amount of time I've spent on this across multiple simulated devices. There's no static value that could work on all devices, and multiplying/dividing them by the device scale hasn't shown any improvements either. 

The direction this PR was heading (as I've attempted to throughly explain in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21335#issuecomment-1364366546, not sure if you read that) is basically turning off size-based scaling (`TargetDrawSize` stuff) on iOS and applying a constant 2x scale to all components of the game instead, which felt pretty good to me as per the screenshots in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21335#issue-1456964765, but the only approach I came up with reads rather horrifying now that I look at it again.

If you think the general direction sounds sane, then I *might* look into improving it later, but definitely don't count on me.

I think what makes the most sense is that we do not increase the *size* of UI elements after a certain resolution is hit, even on desktop. Whether that resolution be 1024x768 or something slightly higher would need some experimentation (on desktop) but I think it's a better approach, especially since we have "UI scale" to allow users to further tweak things to their liking.

Which is to say, this is basically what you did in this PR, but I'd see it being done using a more sane method. I think it may actually be already supported via `DrawSizePreserving` stuff.

issue_context.title: UI scale on iOS is too small by default
issue_context.body:
**Attention**: I intend to work on this issue, preferably with feedback from others.

The following Screenshot is taken on mobile, on a clean build of Osu!Lazer for iOS:
![78165167_3308028942602917_18363759739273216_n](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7114643/69855540-02ce0900-128c-11ea-806a-ff0f98f4bf6d.jpg)

I'm thinking of making a new design, maybe a skin is enough? Where buttons are much larger, as esp. the buttons on the top nav bar are small enough to be a difficult touch target.

Other UX stuff includes difficulties entering the menu inside a game, but that's not 100% related to this.

**Note**: I looked for similar issues, I could comment and work on, but couldn't find any
comments: We are planning on using the same UI across all devices. For now, you can adjust the UI scale (as per the release notes) to make it looks better on mobile devices, but we have no plan on a "separate" design as such.
Would it then make sense to overwrite the default scaling for mobile device, as this is not an immediately discoverable feature?

If we were going to do a proper release, definitely. You're welcome to attempt an implementation to change the default for new installs based on screen size.

For now it is clearly mentioned in the release notes, which display before you run the application.
Since we have the first install setup now, can we close this issue? Scaling is pretty much discovered by all new installation now.
I'd still like to choose a more sane default.

review_comments:
This feels *so* round-about. You're seeing the value here but also reverse setting it using DI on every `Update`? And on iOS the value *is from the scaling container itself*??

I just don't know.
